topic: How are link budgets affected when prioritizing high-revenue services versus navigation safety margins in dynamic scheduling?
consensus_response: In dynamic scheduling, prioritizing high-revenue services over navigation safety margins can lead to reduced link budgets due to increased interference and bandwidth allocation conflicts. The array factor's limitations in dynamic scheduling can compromise navigation signal integrity, necessitating optimized routing algorithms and advanced link management techniques to balance competing demands on link resources. Additionally, Interference Cancellation (IC) techniques can mitigate interference but increase complexity, potentially reducing link budgets.
